title: Focus visibility and logical order
learningObjectives: Explain focus visibility and logical order and apply it to accessible, reliable web development.

understand.concept: Keyboard focus should be clearly visible and follow a logical sequence that matches reading and interaction order. Avoid positive tabindex values and do not remove outlines without providing a strong alternative. Focus management is important for dialogs, menus, and dynamic content.
understand.whyItMatters: Visible focus lets users know where keyboard input will go. A logical order reduces confusion and prevents users from losing their place.
understand.analogy: Focus is the cursor for interaction; it should be visible and move through the page in a sensible route.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; web protocols, browser behaviour, and accessibility requirements follow formal standards and platform implementations.

explain.narrative: The focus-visible rule provides a high-contrast outline when the browser determines visible keyboard focus is appropriate.

examples.explanation: The focus-visible rule provides a high-contrast outline when the browser determines visible keyboard focus is appropriate.
examples.expectedOutput: The example illustrates the concept; some browser examples require a real served page and supported APIs.

practise.guidedTask: Test focus order and indicators on a page. Remove positive tabindex values and ensure focus is not clipped by overflow containers.
practise.independentTask: Apply the concept to a small web page. Record the expected behaviour, how you tested it, and any limitations or fallbacks.
hints: Use browser developer tools to inspect actual behaviour.
Test with keyboard and different viewport sizes.
Keep core content available when enhancements are unsupported.

questions.prompt: What should a developer provide when keyboard focus is on a control?
questions.explanation: Visible focus helps keyboard users identify the active control.

questions.prompt: What is a reliable web engineering habit?
options: Test actual browser behaviour and provide accessible fallbacks
Assume the browser always behaves exactly as expected
questions.answer: Test actual browser behaviour and provide accessible fallbacks
questions.explanation: Reliable web work combines standards knowledge with real testing and inclusive fallbacks.
